atom: QG-40: does the existence/selection separation reproduce in a production compiler?
compiler: Qiskit 2.5.2, optimization_level=1, seed_transpiler=7, line coupling map, 5 qubits
explicitly_not_claimed: that any ORION method beats any production compiler
behaviour at larger qubit counts, other couplings, other optimisation levels, or under seed variance

reading.existence_does_NOT_hold_here: 5 of 10 classes contain circuits with different optimal cost
reading.why_that_differs_from_TARE: TARE's spectrum is the sorted FULL response vector, an information-complete symmetrisation (C1); a degree sequence is far cruder, so the existence half is summary-dependent while the selection half looks generic

recorded_instrument_defect.caught_by: research/extensions/orion-qg/qg40_instrument_validity_check.py, which asks whether the measurement can vary at all
recorded_instrument_defect.effect: cost was constant at every layout (|argmin| = 120/120, range [6,6]) and the experiment reported a VACUOUS clean negative
recorded_instrument_defect.note: a negative from a dead instrument is the failure mode this programme exists to prevent, and it nearly shipped
recorded_instrument_defect.what: the first run counted only cx, while routing expresses its work as inserted swap gates

setup.collisions: built by construction: all 6-edge multigraphs enumerated, deduped by isomorphism, grouped by summary
setup.cost: total two-qubit gates after routing (cx + swap)
setup.summary: (sorted degree sequence, sorted edge-multiplicity multiset), qubit-permutation invariant, no transpiler call
